correctness.rationale: The final claim concerns axial coordinates only. Reconstructed the volume moment v=J_m/I_m and complete surface centroid [a^m+m sqrt((H/R)^2+(1-a)^2) J_{m-1}]/[1+a^m+m sqrt((H/R)^2+(1-a)^2) I_{m-1}] from the tangential base identity R area(∂B)=m vol(B) and the common facet slant factor. Their difference has sign sqrt(t²+(1-a)²)-T_d(a), with ell-v>0 by decreasing weight s, and T_d(a)>1-a by 2J_m>I_m² for the nondegenerate survival-distribution X. This proves a unique positive height crossing and strict trichotomy for all d>=2 and all tangential bases. Checked the endpoint integrals: h_d(0)=sqrt(d²-1), for d=2 h_2²=(a+3)(3a+1), while d>=3 has h_d'(0+)=-sqrt(d²-1) and lim_{a->1}h_d'=2. Interior minimum follows from opposite derivative signs; no uniqueness claimed. Independently recomputed rational I,J and surface-volume signs at t=h/2,h,2h for d=2,...,11 and 4 tapers, rather than relying on the checker log.

value.rationale: The natural question of when a uniform-volume center and complete-boundary area center swap their axial order for a tapered solid has a shape-independent exact answer. The strict interior taper optimum in every dimension at least three is a motivated geometric phase change not merely a classical formula for one frustum. It can be used to benchmark centroid inequalities and geometric sampling.

limitations: Axial equality not full vector equality
Requires a common tangential inball for polytope bases
Prism a=1 is singular: both axial centroids equal for every H despite limiting h->4
Exact global location/uniqueness of interior minimizer not proved
